newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher, Kia worries still linger.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher, Kia worries still linger.

text.p: Stocks ended slightly higher on Monday after a see-saw day on buying of small- and medium-sized shares, which took the worst beating last week, brokers said.
But they said fears of the adverse effects the Kia crisis would have on the economy continued to weigh on the market.

The composite stock index closed 1.60 points higher at 733.92. "Attention is now on the meeting of Kia's creditors on Wednesday," said Kim Choon-kwon of Daewoo Securities. "If the results are not satisfactory, further depression looks inevitable."
Volume was low, with 28.29 million shares changing hands compared with 20.11 million for Saturday's half-day trading. Gainers outpaced losers 426 to 343 with 129 stocks unchanged.
"What clouds the whole atmosphere is that loans for margin trading now exceed customer deposits with securities houses," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Such loans are now estimated at 3.28 trillion won, compared with 3.06 trillion of customer deposits, brokers said.
Taeil Media, a computer parts maker, rose 670 won to its daily upper-limit of 9,060, leading buying of small shares.
Taeil suffered a deep fall last week due to rumours about financial troubles. The company said the rumours were groundless.
Taeil said on Monday it expected its sales would rise to 714.28 billion won this year from 390.54 billion won in 1996.
Net profits were estimated at 17.8 billion won this year, compared with 7.9 billion last year, the company said.
LG Semicon rose to its limit of 44,200 won, up 3,200 won, due to buying by foreigners, who bought about 200,000 shares of the company, brokers said.
"The foreign buying seems to have little to do with semiconductor business. Probably the buying was sparked by the belief that the stock was undervalued," said Chun Tae-min of Dongsuh Securities.
Brokers said the central bank's announcement that the current account deficit had shrunk in June had little impact on the market.
"The results were already anticipated because of the trade ministry's announcement of a trade surplus earlier this month," said Kim of Daewoo.
The central bank reported the current account deficit for June narrowed to $361.4 million from $1.3 billion a year earlier.
